slides.title: The **child's welfare** comes first.
slides.body: When appointing a guardian, the court is guided by what is for the child's welfare. For Hindu children, the law says the child's welfare is the **paramount** consideration.
slides.ref: Guardians and Wards Act 1890 · Sec 17(1); Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act 1956 · Sec 13(1)

slides.title: What the court **looks at.**
list: The child's age, sex and religion
Each proposed guardian's character and capacity
How closely related they are to the child
Their existing or past relations with the child

slides.title: Your child's **wishes** count.
slides.body: If the child is old enough to form an intelligent preference, the court may consider it. In Hindu Marriage Act cases, custody orders follow the children's wishes wherever possible.
slides.ref: Guardians and Wards Act 1890 · Sec 17(3); Hindu Marriage Act 1955 · Sec 26

slides.title: Under 5? **Ordinarily with mother.**
slides.body: For a Hindu boy or unmarried girl, the law names the father, and after him the mother, as natural guardian. But custody of a child under five shall ordinarily be with the mother.
slides.ref: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act 1956 · Sec 6(a) and proviso, 6(b)

slides.title: Custody orders **can change.**
slides.body: In a Hindu Marriage Act case, the court can pass interim custody orders, set custody in the decree, and later revoke, suspend or vary them on a petition.
slides.note: Uttarakhand: State's Uniform Civil Code applies

slides.title: Where do you **file?**
slides.body: Cases on guardianship, custody of a child, or **access** (visiting rights) go to the Family Court, where one has been set up for your area.
slides.ref: Family Courts Act 1984 · Sec 7(1) Explanation (g), Sec 8

sources: Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 – Section 17 (as quoted in Nil Ratan Kundu v. Abhijit Kundu, Supreme Court, 2008)
Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 – Sections 4(a), 6, 13
caption:
Divorce and children: who decides custody, and how? 👇

1️⃣ The child's welfare comes first; for Hindu children it is the paramount consideration
2️⃣ The court looks at the child's age, sex and religion, and each guardian's character, capacity and relationship with the child
3️⃣ If the child is old enough to form an intelligent preference, the court may consider it
4️⃣ For a Hindu child under five, custody shall ordinarily be with the mother
5️⃣ Custody orders in Hindu Marriage Act cases can later be revoked, suspended or varied
6️⃣ Custody and visiting-rights cases go to the Family Court, where one exists
⚠️ In Uttarakhand, the State's Uniform Civil Code, 2024 now governs marriage and divorce of residents (except Scheduled Tribes)

Source: Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (Sec 17); Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 (Sec 6, 13); Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (Sec 26); Family Courts Act, 1984 (Sec 7, 8)
